identity: Gor Drazhak musters the Throng; round its walls scorpions, hyenas and a bandit ration-broker take their cut.

quests.title: Our Word, Our Witness
quests.text: Rokka Emberhand's report from Redtusk tells of herders charged for water they had already carried before it was stolen. Take the case to Drava Flintshoulder of The Oathdelvers at the Miner's Guild house here in Gor Drazhak. She keeps the guild's delivery pledges with the army's suppliers. The people waiting for water deserve to hear whose promise is being sold back to them.
quests.completion: I'll take this up with our suppliers and put Rokka's account beside the delivery pledges. When The Oathdelvers promise a load, we stand by it. No one gets to turn our kept word into a debt for the people we supplied.

variants.text: Word from Raincall says a rain tithe taken under threat is being called the community's own promise. Take it to Ombali Ropekeeper of The Oathdelvers at the Miner's Guild house here in Kezamba. She checks the witnesses' accounts with the army's suppliers, and knows to ask what those witnesses actually saw. A frightened payment should not be allowed to speak for a whole village.
variants.completion: I will check that claimed promise with our suppliers and keep Veko's refusal in the account. A witness can tell us what happened; someone writing beneath their name afterwards cannot add to what they saw. We will start there.

variants.text: The report from Mournfen describes remains carried away from their names, with strangers claiming the right to take them. Speak to Iven Lastshift of The Oathdelvers at the Miner's Guild house here in Nhal Veyr. He checks the guild's records with the army's suppliers and will examine those claims. Someone should still be able to say who the missing were.
variants.completion: I will keep the names with this case and check the claims against our supply records. A register preserves a person for us to remember; it does not put them at the disposal of whoever next opens the book. Sera's report will be heard.

quests.lesson: Chapter 1 opens at the envoy at 19 with no prerequisite; a walk to the capital's Miner's Guild house.

quests.title: Whose Word Is This?
quests.text: The army's suppliers and I have stopped a disputed handover at Gor Drazhak's water depot. Someone has copied the recipients and witnesses onto a new demand for payment or service, as though receiving water meant agreeing to work it off. Secure the original witness record at the depot on the edge of the cook court and bring your findings back to me. I know what The Oathdelvers promised, and I intend to see it delivered.
quests.completion: These witnesses confirmed a delivery, and I have struck the added demand out in front of everyone waiting at the depot. Our suppliers will issue the water as The Oathdelvers pledged it, with no new debt to its recipients. We still need to learn how the records reached those making the claim; similar misuse of old names is reported in Ossuary Reach.

variants.text: Here in Kezamba, someone has taken a witnessed act of unloading and claimed the helpers promised their labour whenever called. Our suppliers and I have paused the disputed handover so we can settle that claim before the porters' stores are issued. Secure the original witness record at the landing beside the shore store, then return to me. Helping with one load should not mean carrying every load that follows.
variants.completion: The witnesses saw one unloading, and I have struck out the claim of further work where the porters could hear it. The suppliers will release the porters' stores under the original agreement. Who obtained the records for this misuse is still unknown; reports from Ossuary Reach describe old names being made to answer for new claims.

variants.text: Personal belongings await their recipients in the receiving court outside Nhal Veyr's mourners' hall. Someone has used genuine register entries to claim a debt against them, and our suppliers and I have stopped the disputed handover for examination. Secure the original witness record there and return to me. I want the names preserved and the claimed debt accounted for separately.
variants.completion: The names establish whom these belongings should reach; the added debt has no basis, and I strike it out before the mourners. Our suppliers will release the belongings to the recorded recipients with those names intact. We have yet to learn how the claimant obtained the records, and reports from Ossuary Reach suggest older names are suffering the same treatment.

quests.lesson: A spot in the capital town (a town place) and back; the leader decides the capital's case, the papers' source stays open.

quests.title: A Sentry Needs Both Feet
quests.text: Dust Stingers come out on the {name:steppe} at night, and a sentry with a swollen foot is no use chasing trouble. Kill three and report to me. I have told the recruits to check their boots; now I need someone to check the ground beyond them.
quests.lesson: A short night hunt; a third of a day hunt's count.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: a new id (its objectives changed); free play, a level only.

quests.title: Lunch Is Not Included
quests.text: Dustpack Hyenas have learnt that a marching recruit carries lunch and may be persuaded to drop it. Kill eight by day in the {name:badlands}. The recruits are here to learn soldiering, and I would prefer the hyenas stopped taking part in the lessons.
quests.lesson: A day hunt in the badlands.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the id stays (objectives unchanged); free play, a level only.

quests.title: His Profit, Our Empty Bowls
quests.text: Bandit Ration-Broker Garr buys the supplies Korr steals from Redtusk and sells our own rations back to hungry people. Kill Garr at the {name:tollcamp}, {dir_from_giver:tollcamp}, and bring me word. He calls himself a broker because it sounds better than admitting whose bowls he empties.
quests.completion: Garr's profit ends there. I will make sure the crews hear that his demands carried no promise of ours.
quests.lesson: The capital's named leader at his camp, alone: the capital's local finale.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: a new id (its objectives changed); free play, a level only.

quests.title: Spears Out, Word Back
quests.text: Brakka Jarward at Speargrass Wellhold feeds the crews and notices every empty place when they come home. Go and offer her a hand in Speargrass Reach. She needs people who pay attention before the meal is served.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the handover id stays; free play, it requires nothing and claims no earlier deed (draft §10).

quests.title: Salt Keeps a Friendship
quests.text: Taleko Drycord at Whisperreed Landing keeps goods moving between our people, including the salt that makes my cooking worth boasting about. Take my regards to him in the Whispering Reedlands and ask what help he needs. A friendship should carry something useful in both directions.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the handover id stays; free play, it requires nothing and claims no earlier deed (draft §10).

quests.title: Your Place in the Line
quests.text: Drek Rampbinder on Bannerbreak Mesa needs help keeping The Throng's line supplied and standing. Go and report to him. Tell him you came ready to work; he can decide where your hands are needed.
quests.notes: Round 60 CAPITALS: the handover id stays; free play, it requires nothing and claims no earlier deed (draft §10).
